words.definitionEn: a sign of illness that a patient notices
words.collocations: a common symptom · mild symptoms · develop symptoms
words.example: The first symptom was a dry cough that would not stop.

words.definitionEn: medical care given to cure or manage an illness
words.collocations: receive treatment · effective treatment · treatment for
words.example: Early treatment makes the recovery much shorter.

words.definitionEn: stopping a problem before it happens
words.collocations: prevention is better than cure · disease prevention
words.example: Vaccination is the cheapest form of prevention.

words.definitionEn: lasting a long time and hard to cure
words.collocations: chronic illness · chronic pain · chronic shortage
words.example: Chronic illness costs families more than acute illness.

words.definitionEn: the measured amount of a medicine taken at one time
words.collocations: a daily dose · increase the dose
words.example: Taking a double dose does not make the medicine work faster.

words.definitionEn: the body's ability to resist an infection
words.collocations: build immunity · immunity to
words.example: Immunity after an infection does not always last forever.

words.definitionEn: the food a person needs to stay healthy
words.collocations: good nutrition · poor nutrition
words.example: Good nutrition supports recovery as much as medicine does.

words.definitionEn: a disease spreading quickly through a population
words.collocations: an epidemic of · tackle an epidemic
words.example: The epidemic forced schools to close for a month.

words.definitionEn: an unwanted result caused by a medicine
words.collocations: a common side effect · suffer side effects
words.example: Drowsiness is a common side effect of that drug.

words.definitionEn: the identification of an illness by a doctor
words.collocations: make a diagnosis · an early diagnosis
words.example: A late diagnosis makes treatment harder and more expensive.

words.definitionEn: a move to a more important job in the same organisation
words.collocations: earn a promotion · a promotion to
words.example: She earned the promotion after leading two projects.

words.definitionEn: the time by which work must be finished
words.collocations: meet a deadline · miss a deadline
words.example: The deadline was moved forward, so the team worked late.

words.definitionEn: the amount of work one person has to do
words.collocations: a heavy workload · manage the workload
words.example: A heavy workload is not the same as a productive one.

words.definitionEn: a person you work with
words.collocations: a close colleague · work with colleagues
words.example: A supportive colleague can make a difficult job bearable.

words.definitionEn: a period of training work, often for students
words.collocations: a paid internship · do an internship
words.example: The internship turned into her first permanent role.

words.definitionEn: payment for work done
words.collocations: fair remuneration · remuneration package
words.example: Remuneration matters, but it is rarely the only reason people stay.

words.definitionEn: a schedule the employee can partly choose
words.collocations: offer flexible hours · work flexible hours
words.example: Flexible hours help parents stay in skilled work.

words.definitionEn: the rate at which staff leave and are replaced
words.collocations: high staff turnover · reduce turnover
words.example: High turnover usually signals a problem in management.

words.definitionEn: losing a job because the role is no longer needed
words.collocations: face redundancy · voluntary redundancy
words.example: Redundancy is rarely the employee's fault.

words.definitionEn: a formal review of an employee's performance
words.collocations: an annual appraisal · a performance appraisal
words.example: An annual appraisal is more useful when it happens twice a year.
